sentences.en: For six decades, until his death last week, Stephen Sondheim transformed musical theater into an art form as rich, complex, and contradictory as life itself.
sentences.zh: 六十年间，直到上周去世，斯蒂芬·桑德海姆将音乐剧变成了一种如同生活本身一样丰富、复杂且充满矛盾的艺术形式。

sentences.en: If it's unnecessary, then the show generally turns out to be not very good.

sentences.en: I spoke with my colleague, theater critic Jesse Green, about Sondheim's career, influence, and legacy.
sentences.zh: 我采访了我的同事、戏剧评论家杰西·格林，探讨了桑德海姆的职业生涯、影响力和遗产。

sentences.en: What was your first real encounter with his work?
sentences.zh: 你对他的作品的第一次真正接触是什么时候？

sentences.en: I suppose it was when I was about 11, and my parents, who used to go from where I lived in the suburbs of Philadelphia to New York now and then to see shows, my mother had been
sentences.zh: 我想那是我大约11岁的时候，我的父母过去常常从我居住的费城郊区偶尔去纽约看演出，我母亲当时

sentences.en: really turned on by hair, as whose was not, really.
sentences.zh: 真的被《毛发》迷住了，就像当时几乎所有人一样。

sentences.en: Hair the musical, not the thing on your head.

sentences.zh: 有一天深夜，他们看完某场演出回来，还在一直讨论，这已经是在两小时的车程回家之后了。

sentences.en: And they were like, oh my God, this is incredible.
sentences.zh: 他们当时的状态是，哦天哪，这太不可思议了。

sentences.en: I'd never heard them talk about a show as if it were, say, a novel.
sentences.zh: 我以前从未听过他们像讨论一本小说那样讨论一部演出。

sentences.en: And so which show had they just seen?
sentences.zh: 那他们刚看的是哪部剧呢？

sentences.en: The name of the show was Company, which I then learned was a new musical by Stephen Sondheim that had opened in 1970 on Broadway.
sentences.zh: 这部剧的名字叫《公司》，我后来了解到这是斯蒂芬·桑德海姆的一部新音乐剧，于1970年在百老汇上演。

sentences.en: And my parents had bought at the theater the cassette tape, and I played it, and then I played it again.
sentences.zh: 我父母在剧院买了一盘盒式磁带，我播放了它，然后又播放了一遍。

sentences.en: I just needed to know how this was done, who these people were, who made it, and how they
sentences.zh: 我只是想知道这是怎么做出来的，这些人是谁，是谁创作的，以及他们

sentences.en: made it, how the show was having the effects it was having on me, even though I was, whatever,
sentences.zh: 是如何制作的，为什么这部剧会对我产生这样的影响，尽管我当时不管怎么说，

sentences.zh: 只有11岁，而剧里讲的是一群互相之间有点刻薄的成熟曼哈顿人。

sentences.en: And I didn't know anything about that world, but I wanted to.
sentences.zh: 我对那个世界一无所知，但我很想了解。

sentences.en: And so what I did was I took out a legal pad, and I listened, and I copied every word of the entire show.
sentences.zh: 所以我做的事情是，拿出一个法律专用的黄色记事本，一边听一边把整部剧的每个字都抄了下来。

sentences.en: It took several listenings.
sentences.zh: 这听了好几遍才完成。

sentences.en: And finally got the entire thing down on paper.
sentences.zh: 最后把整部剧都落实到了纸上。

sentences.en: That's the only way I could...
sentences.zh: 那是唯一能让我……

sentences.en: You transcribed the entire production.
sentences.zh: 你把整部作品都手抄下来了。

sentences.en: The entire cast album.
sentences.zh: 整个卡司专辑。

sentences.zh: 用手抄的。

sentences.en: In longhand.

sentences.zh: 这是我唯一能想到的方法，来吸收其中蕴含的情感、想法和精湛技艺。

sentences.en: I don't know many 11-year-olds who sit down and transcribe longhand a Broadway musical.
sentences.zh: 我不认识多少11岁的孩子会坐下来手抄一部百老汇音乐剧。

sentences.en: Well, I also used to be paid a quarter to organize the drawers at the synagogue.
sentences.zh: 好吧，我以前整理犹太教堂的抽屉还能赚到二十五美分呢。

sentences.en: So, you know, I was just a strange kid.
sentences.zh: 所以，你知道的，我只是个奇怪的小孩。

sentences.en: Well, let's just pause for a minute and help me understand this man, Stephen Sondheim, who
sentences.zh: 好吧，让我们暂停一会儿，帮我了解这个人——斯蒂芬·桑德海姆，他在你

sentences.en: was transfixing you at the age of 11, and how it was that he became such a legendary figure in musical theater.
sentences.zh: 11岁时就让你着迷，以及他是如何成为音乐剧界如此传奇的人物。

sentences.en: Well, in the simplest outline, he was an incredibly smart New York kid from a troubled family.
sentences.zh: 简而言之，他是一个来自问题家庭、聪明得不可思议的纽约小孩。

sentences.en: When I was 10 years old, my parents divorced, my mother got custody of me, and she bought a place in Doylestown, Pennsylvania.
sentences.zh: 在我10岁时，我父母离婚了，我母亲获得了我的抚养权，并在宾夕法尼亚州的多伊尔斯敦买了一处房产。

sentences.en: Moved part-time out to Bucks County, Pennsylvania, near the home of Oscar Hammerstein, the great
sentences.zh: 我们搬到了宾夕法尼亚州巴克斯县过半隐居的生活，靠近奥斯卡·汉默斯坦的家，他是伟大的

sentences.en: lyricist and book writer who, you know, wrote Showboat in Oklahoma and The Sound of Music and many other shows.
sentences.zh: 词作家和剧本作家，你知道的，他写过《演艺船》、《俄克拉荷马》、《音乐之声》和许多其他剧目。

sentences.en: And very quickly, maybe because of his own need for a father figure in his life, because
sentences.zh: 很快，也许是因为他内心对父爱形象的渴望，因为

sentences.en: he didn't ever really see his father, he glommed on with a special attachment to Hammerstein.
sentences.zh: 他从来没有真正见过自己的父亲，他特别依恋地黏上了汉默斯坦。

sentences.en: And he became a surrogate father, and I just wanted to do what he did.
sentences.zh: 他成了他的代父，而我只想做他所做的事。

sentences.en: And therefore, to whatever it was that Hammerstein could teach him.
sentences.zh: 因此，去学习汉默斯坦能教给他的任何东西。

sentences.en: If he was a geologist, I would have become a geologist, which is, I'm sure, an exaggeration, but not much.
sentences.zh: 如果他是个地质学家，我也会成为一名地质学家，这当然有点夸张，但也差不太多。

sentences.en: And Hammerstein proceeded to do, in a series of complicated exercises and assignments, the first one being an adaptation of a play that I thought was good, the second being an
sentences.zh: 汉默斯坦开始通过一系列复杂的练习和作业来教导他——第一个是对一部我认为不错的剧本进行改编，第二个是

sentences.en: adaptation of a play that I liked but was flawed, was to teach him what was then the state of the art of the American musical theater, but limited in some ways by what Hammerstein
sentences.zh: 对一部我喜欢但有缺陷的剧本进行改编——以此向他传授当时美国音乐剧的最高水平，但在某些方面也受限于汉默斯坦

sentences.en: knew.
sentences.zh: 所知的局限。

sentences.en: And as great as he was, there was a lot, as Sondheim later came to realize, that he didn't know.
sentences.zh: 尽管他如此伟大，正如桑德海姆后来意识到的那样，也有很多是他所不知道的。

sentences.en: Well, explain that.
sentences.zh: 好吧，解释一下。

sentences.en: What would Hammerstein have known?
sentences.zh: 汉默斯坦会知道些什么？

sentences.en: What would have been the hallmarks of his work and of musical theater in this moment, as a young Stephen Sondheim is starting this apprenticeship?
sentences.zh: 作为一个年轻的斯蒂芬·桑德海姆开始这段学徒生涯时，他的作品和当时的音乐剧会有什么标志性的特征？

sentences.en: In a typical Hammerstein show, not unlike a typical sitcom today, you have an A plot, you have a B plot that's contrasting, usually humorous.
sentences.zh: 在典型的汉默斯坦音乐剧中，与今天的典型情景喜剧没什么不同，你有一条A线剧情，一条与之形成对比的B线剧情，通常很幽默。

sentences.en: You may have a C plot.
sentences.zh: 你可能还有一条C线剧情。

sentences.en: And how these all are worked out and what songs have to exist in what places in a show.
sentences.zh: 所有这些是如何运作的，以及什么歌曲必须存在于剧中的什么位置。

sentences.en: All of these kinds of things which have been codified more or less now are things that he
sentences.zh: 所有这些现在或多或少已经成文的规范，都是他

sentences.en: invented and was able to teach Sondheim, almost like teaching a painter, you know, how to make a canvas.
sentences.zh: 发明并能够传授给桑德海姆的，几乎就像教一个画家如何制作画布一样。

sentences.en: But Jesse, you said Sondheim understood, even as he was learning all of this from Hammerstein, that something was missing from this era of the musical.
sentences.zh: 但是杰西，你刚才说过，桑德海姆甚至在向汉默斯坦学习这一切时，就明白这个时期的音乐剧缺少了某些东西。

sentences.en: So what did he feel was missing?
sentences.zh: 那么他觉得缺少了什么？

sentences.en: Complexity.
sentences.zh: 复杂性。

sentences.en: Hammerstein, you know, famously rhymes a lot of very simple words.
sentences.zh: 众所周知，汉默斯坦押韵了许多非常简单的词。

sentences.en: He was capable of trickier rhymes, but they're often about birds praying or something like that, you know, you know, and storms and lifting your chin up high.
sentences.zh: 他有能力写出更巧妙的押韵，但它们通常是关于祈祷的鸟儿之类的内容，你知道的，还有风暴和高高昂起你的下巴。

sentences.en: But Sondheim as a young man was already like very deeply into wordplay and other kinds of complex ideas about language and sound.
sentences.zh: 但桑德海姆年轻时就已经深深着迷于双关语以及关于语言和声音的其他各种复杂理念。

sentences.en: And I think he knew this about himself and understood that the forms that Hammerstein was teaching him about were just never going to give him the full opportunity to express what
sentences.zh: 我想他很了解自己这一点，并明白汉默斯坦教给他的那些形式永远无法完全给他提供表达他内心想法的

sentences.en: he had in him.
sentences.zh: 广阔机会。

sentences.en: And when it came into his hands to possibly write the lyrics for West Side Story, he did not want to do it.
sentences.zh: 当他有机会可能为《西区故事》填词时，他其实并不想做。

sentences.en: I had no intention of just writing lyrics.
sentences.zh: 我根本没打算只写歌词。

sentences.en: I want to write music.
sentences.zh: 我想写音乐。

sentences.en: And I called Oscar, who's, you know, my advisor on everything.
sentences.zh: 我打电话给奥斯卡，你知道的，他是我所有事情的顾问。

sentences.en: And I said, you know, I don't want to do this.
sentences.zh: 我说，你知道的，我不想做这个。

sentences.en: But Oscar said, look, you have a chance to work with very gifted professionals on a show that sounds interesting.
sentences.zh: 但奥斯卡说，听着，你有机会在一部听起来很有趣的剧里与非常有天赋的专业人士合作。

sentences.en: He said, my advice would be to take the job.
sentences.zh: 他说，我的建议是接受这份工作。

sentences.en: Hammerstein said, this is another lesson.
sentences.zh: 汉默斯坦说，这是又一课。

sentences.en: You have to learn how to write for this kind of composer, Leonard Bernstein, and how to write for this kind of show.
sentences.zh: 你必须学会如何为这种类型的作曲家伦纳德·伯恩斯坦写歌，以及如何为这种类型的剧集写歌。

sentences.en: To set up dances and all the different things that this show would present.
sentences.zh: 为舞蹈以及这部剧将呈现的所有不同元素做好铺垫。

sentences.en: So he did take the job.
sentences.zh: 所以他确实接下了这份工作。

sentences.en: And he was, in fact, not satisfied with his work on it.
sentences.zh: 而且，事实上，他对自己在其中的工作并不满意。

sentences.en: Lenny wanted everything, the lyrics to be very poetic.
sentences.zh: 伦尼希望一切都好，歌词要非常富有诗意。

sentences.en: But his idea of poetry and my idea of poetry are simply not the same.
sentences.zh: 但他对诗歌的理解和我对诗歌的理解简直不是一回事。

sentences.en: I mean, you know, I was 25 years old.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，你知道的，我当时25岁。

sentences.en: Even though we recognize the greatness of the show, what he hears when he sees it, and he's often spoken about this in interviews, is the discontinuity between who the characters
sentences.zh: 尽管我们承认这部剧的伟大，但当他看到它时听到的，并且他经常在采访中谈到这一点，是角色本身

sentences.en: are and often the way they sing.
sentences.zh: 与他们唱歌的方式之间存在着脱节。

sentences.en: So you have a character like Maria, who has recently come to New York from Puerto Rico and doesn't speak a great deal of English.
sentences.zh: 比如玛丽亚这个角色，她最近从波多黎各来到纽约，并不怎么会说英语。

sentences.en: But when she sings, she sings like she's at a tea party at Noel Coward's house.
sentences.zh: 但当她唱歌时，她唱得就像在诺埃尔·科沃德家的茶会上一样。

sentences.en: I feel charming, oh so charming.
sentences.zh: 我觉得自己好迷人，哦，好迷人。

sentences.en: It's alarming how charming I feel.
sentences.zh: 我觉得自己迷人得惊人。

sentences.en: It's alarming how charming I feel.
sentences.zh: 我觉得自己迷人得惊人。

sentences.en: Sondheim hated that line.
sentences.zh: 桑德海姆讨厌那句台词。

sentences.en: It isn't that he thought the show was no good.
sentences.zh: 这倒不是说他认为这部剧不好。

sentences.en: It's that he felt that his lyrics were not what they could have been and the show was not what he might have done if he were doing both music and lyrics.
sentences.zh: 而是他觉得自己的歌词没有达到应有的水准，如果是由他同时负责词曲创作，这部剧本可以呈现出更好的效果。

sentences.en: So when does he finally have a chance to do things the Sondheim way, on his own terms, with all the complexity that he wants musical theater to possess?
sentences.zh: 那么他究竟是什么时候才真正有机会以桑德海姆的方式、按照他自己的条件、带着他希望音乐剧拥有的全部复杂性来做事情呢？

sentences.en: Well, the 60s were a frustrating continuation of his apprenticeship, even if he was writing his own music and lyrics in a couple of shows.
sentences.zh: 嗯，60年代是他学徒生涯中令人沮丧的延续，哪怕他在几部剧中创作了自己的词曲。

sentences.en: It wasn't really until the other show we talked about already, Company, in 1970, which he wrote
sentences.zh: 直到我们前面已经讨论过的另一部剧《公司》（1970年），他为该剧作词作曲并深度参与了构思，

sentences.en: the music and the lyrics for and was strongly involved in the conception of, that we finally begin to hear the mature sound of the Sondheim we now know.
sentences.zh: 我们才终于开始听到我们现在所熟知的那个成熟的桑德海姆的声音。

sentences.en: So tell us why Company feels like such a breakthrough.
sentences.zh: 那么请告诉我们为什么《公司》会让人觉得是一次如此重大的突破。

sentences.en: Well, for one thing, it barely has a plot.
sentences.zh: 嗯，首先，它几乎没有什么剧情。

sentences.en: And that sounds like it might be a criticism, but from Sondheim's point of view, what that means is there's a lot of room for him and for the songs to take on structural weight,
sentences.zh: 这听起来可能像是一种批评，但从桑德海姆的角度来看，这意味着他和歌曲有很大的空间来承载结构上的分量，

sentences.en: not just decorative weight.
sentences.zh: 而不仅仅是装饰性的分量。

sentences.en: It's a story about a 35-year-old guy who's single and afraid of commitment and his five married couples who are his friends urging him to get married.
sentences.zh: 这是一个关于35岁单身汉的故事，他害怕承诺，而他作为朋友的五对已婚夫妇则敦促他结婚。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: So that's really the entire story of the musical, and the weight of what it's trying to say isn't on the plot.
sentences.zh: 所以这确实是音乐剧的全部故事，而它想要表达的分量并不在剧情上。

sentences.en: It's on the songs to excavate character and the layers of contrasting feelings within Bobby, the main character, but also the people around him.
sentences.zh: 它在于通过歌曲来挖掘主角鲍比内心深处的人物性格和多层相反的情感，以及他身边的人。

sentences.en: So we are in a world of feelings that's expressly about feelings, not about events.
sentences.zh: 所以我们置身于一个纯粹关于情感而非事件的世界中。

sentences.en: And you hear that in a lot of the songs in the show, but never so much as in the big finale
sentences.zh: 你在剧中的许多歌曲中都能听到这一点，但尤其是在为鲍比创作的大型压轴曲目

sentences.en: number for Bobby called Being Alive, in which he's going to have to resolve what it is he wants.
sentences.zh: 《活着》中表现得淋漓尽致，在这首歌中，他将不得不理清自己真正想要的是什么。

sentences.en: And the way he does it is quite brilliant.
sentences.zh: 他这样做的方式相当精彩。

sentences.en: It's structural.
sentences.zh: 这是结构性的。
